Award/Judgment Factual Position & Pleadings
1. A Dar was filed on 23/10/2017 by Investigation Officer (Io) before my Ld. Predecessor in the
presence of all the parties of this case.
The Dar was prepared by Io in re
spect of a motor vehicular accident which occurred at about 4:30 PM on 16/08/2017 at a spot situated Near Laxmi Niwas Ashram,
Pusta LOVLEEN Date: 2023.01.17 Road, Jharoda, Burari, Delhi in which one Shivam Kumar Jha S/o Lal Babu Jha (hereinafter referred to as "petitioner") sustained grievous injuries.

As per DAR, at the relevant time, the petitioner was walking to his home when he was hit by a motorcycle bearing registration no. DL-5SAZ-0814(hereinafter referred to as "offending vehicle")
which was coming from the direction of Jharoda Chowki at a high speed.
Petitioner fell down and sustained injuries in his left foot and head.
The motorcyclist namely Deepak Kumar immediately removed the petitioner to Kayakalp Hospital for medical treatment, from where the petitioner was referred to Trauma Centre Hospital.
On the very next day i.e. 17/08/2017 petitioner developed headache and was shifted to LNJP hospital where he underwent a surgery in the head.

An FIR no.
446/17 PS Burari U/s 279/337 IPC was registered at the instance of petitioner wherein he stated that the accident took place on account of rashness and negligence of the motorcyclist.
R-1 is the rider of the offending vehicle and R-2 is the owner of the offending vehicle.
R-3 is the insurer of the offending vehicle.
DAR was treated as a 'claim petition'.
R 3/insurance company was directed to file a legal offer/reasoned decision in response to the said DAR.
R1 and R2 were also directed to file their Written Statements.
Petitioner was also directed to file statement of facts in the prescribed Form G. LOVLEEN Date: 2023.01.17 2.
A WS was filed by R-1 claiming that he was falsely implicated in the present case as the offending vehicle was never involved in any accident as claimed by the petitioner.
R-1 claims that at the relevant time the petitioner was chasing a kite and in the process was hit by a white coloured Santro Car which fled the spot.
R-1 further claims that he stopped his vehicle on humanitarian grounds.
just to assist the petitioner.

However, R-1 states that the offending vehicle was covered by an insurance policy issued by R-3/ Insurance Company and as such, the liability, if any, is to be borne by R-3/

9. It is well settled that the procedure followed for proceedings conducted by an accident tribunal is similar to that followed by a civil court and in civil matters the facts are required to be established by preponderance of probabilities only and not by strict rules of evidence or beyond reasonable doubts as are required in a criminal prosecution.

The burden of proof in a civil case is never as heavy as that is required in a criminal case, but in a claim petition under the Motor Vehicles Act, this burden is infact even lesser than that in a civil case.

Reference in this regard can be made to the propositions of law laid down by the Hon'ble Supreme Court in the case of Bimla Devi and others Vs. Himachal Road Transport Corporation and others, reported in (2009) 13 SC 530, which were reiterated in the subsequent judgment in the case of Parmeshwari Vs. sentences.text: As already discussed above, the petitioner examined his father Sh. Lal Babu Jha as PW-1 in this regard.

PW-1 deposed, vide his affidavit Ex.PW1/1, that the petitioner sustained injuries in an accident that took place on 16/08/2017 LOVLEEN Date:
when the offending vehicle had hit him.

Inter-alia, PW-1 placed on record a copy of FIR Ex. PW1/B, which was registered at the instance of petitioner himself, wherein the petitioner had stated that the accident took place on account of rashness and negligence of R-1.
Admittedly, R-1 and R-2 have not bothered to contest the above claim of the petitioner as to the facts and circumstances leading to the occurrence of the accident.

Admittedly, R-3/ Insurance Company had offered a sum of Rs. 55,000/-
as compensation to the petitioner in the beginning of this enquiry.

11. The very fact that R-1 has already been chargesheeted for the offences punishable under Sections 279/338 IPC in the above criminal case/FIR in itself is a strong circumstance to support the above oral testimony of PW1 and the case of petitioner on this issue.

The copies of FIR, Charge- sheet, Site plan, Mechanical inspection report of offending vehicle, MLC, Seizure Memos, Arrest Memo of R-1 also corroborate the oral testimony of PW1.
12.

Besides the above, R-1 himself was the best witness who could have stepped into the witness box to challenge the depositions being made by PW1 regarding the above accident and its manner etc.,
but he has not done so.

Therefore, an adverse inference on this aspect is also required to be drawn against the respondents in view of the law laid down in case of LOVLEEN Date: 2023.01.17 Cholamandalam M.S. General Insurance Company Ltd. Vs. Kamlesh, reported in 2009 (3) AD (Delhi) 310.
13.
In view of the above, it could be safely assumed that the petitioner was hit at the relevant time by the offending vehicle which R-1 was riding.

14. Having ruled so, this Tribunal now proceeds to assess the wrongful act, neglect or default of R-1,
if any, in driving the offending vehicle at the relevant time.
Admittedly, R-1 has not explained the circumstances under which his vehicle (i.e. The offending vehicle) hit the petitioner at the relevant time.

In the absence of any averment or evidence regarding any mechanical defect in the offending vehicle or any negligent/sudden movement on the part of the petitioner, the only inference possible in the given facts and circumstances is that of neglect and default on the part of R-1 in riding the offending vehicle at the relevant time.
In view of the above discussion, this tribunal is constrained to hold R-1 guilty of gross neglect and default in riding the offending vehicle at the relevant time.
15. In view of the medical treatment documents placed on record by the petitioner, no dispute is left regarding the nature of injuries sustained by him in the above accident.

17. As the issue no.1 has been proved in affirmative and in favour of the petitioner, the petitioner has become entitled to be compensated for the injuries suffered in the above accident, but the computation of compensation and liability to pay the same are required to be decided.
Here it would be appropriate to mention that the petitioner was a minor on the date of accident.

As such, the matter requires decision in accordance with the observations made by the Hon'ble Supreme Court of India in Mallikarjun vs. Divisional Manager, The National Insurance Company Limited and Ors.

hardship, inconvenience, and discomfort, etc., and loss of amenities in life on account of permanent disability 18.

As per discharge summary Ex. PW1/E, the petitioner was diagnosed to be suffering from 'Lt T' P'
EDH with Fracture of Rt Tibia' and he underwent 'Decompression + evaluation of EDH'.

As per disability certificate Ex. PW1/H, petitioner is a case of : Head Injury (operated) and Fracture of Left Tibia and has sustained permanent disability to the LOVLEEN Date:
extent of 75% from 'psychiatry side'.
There is no material available on record so as to assist this Tribunal in the assessment of disability of the petitioner with respect to his whole body.
In the facts and circumstances, it would be appropriate to presume that the petitioner is suffering from 50% disability with respect to his whole body.

Hence,
keeping in view the observations made in Mallikarjun (supra) the petitioner is held entitled to a sum of Rs. 4,00,000/- with respect to the disability suffered by him in the accident.

(iii) Loss of Marriage Prospects 21.
Admittedly, the petitioner would soon attain "majority".
Admittedly, petitioner had to undergo a lot of trauma and pain on account of the above accident when he was just 11 years old.
He also suffered a permanent disability to the extent of 75% from psychiatry side.
This Tribunal could not turn a blind eye to the fact that the above disability is very much likely to affect the marriage prospects of the petitioner.
As such, the petitioner is granted a sum of Rs. 2,00,000/ under this head as well.
(iv) Medical and incidental expenses during the period of hospitalization 22.
The petitioner has placed on judicial file his medical bills, which are Ex. PW1/G.

opennyai_summary.facts:
Petitioner fell down and sustained injuries in his left foot and head.
On the very next day i.e. 17/08/2017 petitioner developed headache and was shifted to LNJP hospital where he underwent a surgery in the head.
opennyai_summary.ANALYSIS:
9. It is well settled that the procedure followed for proceedings conducted by an accident tribunal is similar to that followed by a civil court and in civil matters the facts are required to be established by preponderance of probabilities only and not by strict rules of evidence or beyond reasonable doubts as are required in a criminal prosecution.
The burden of proof in a civil case is never as heavy as that is required in a criminal case, but in a claim petition under the Motor Vehicles Act, this burden is infact even lesser than that in a civil case.
Reference in this regard can be made to the propositions of law laid down by the Hon'ble Supreme Court in the case of Bimla Devi and others Vs. Himachal Road Transport Corporation and others, reported in (2009) 13 SC 530, which were reiterated in the subsequent judgment in the case of Parmeshwari Vs. Amir Chand and others 2011 (1) SCR 1096 Shivam Kumar Jha vs Deepak Kumar on 17 January, 2023 Indian Kanoon - http://indiankanoon.org/doc/64112496/
5 (Civil Appeal No.1082 of 2011) and also recently in another case Mangla Ram Vs. Oriental Insurance Co. Ltd. & Ors., 2018 Law Suit (SC) 303.
10.
Therefore, an adverse inference on this aspect is also required to be drawn against the respondents in view of the law laid down in case of LOVLEEN Date: 2023.01.17 Cholamandalam M.S. General Insurance Company Ltd. Vs. Kamlesh, reported in 2009 (3) AD (Delhi) 310.
13.
In view of the above, it could be safely assumed that the petitioner was hit at the relevant time by the offending vehicle which R-1 was riding.
Admittedly, R-1 has not explained the circumstances under which his vehicle (i.e. The offending vehicle) hit the petitioner at the relevant time.
In the absence of any averment or evidence regarding any mechanical defect in the offending vehicle or any negligent/sudden movement on the part of the petitioner, the only inference possible in the given facts and circumstances is that of neglect and default on the part of R-1 in riding the offending vehicle at the relevant time.
In view of the above discussion, this tribunal is constrained to hold R-1 guilty of gross neglect and default in riding the offending vehicle at the relevant time.
15. In view of the medical treatment documents placed on record by the petitioner, no dispute is left regarding the nature of injuries sustained by him in the above accident.

In view of the above discussion, this Tribunal holds that the petitioner suffered grievous injuries on his person on account of neglect and default of R-1 while riding the offending vehicle at the relevant time.
17. As the issue no.1 has been proved in affirmative and in favour of the petitioner, the petitioner has become entitled to be compensated for the injuries suffered in the above accident, but the computation of compensation and liability to pay the same are required to be decided.
As per disability certificate Ex. PW1/H, petitioner is a case of : Head Injury (operated) and Fracture of Left Tibia and has sustained permanent disability to the LOVLEEN Date:
extent of 75% from 'psychiatry side'.
There is no material available on record so as to assist this Tribunal in the assessment of disability of the petitioner with respect to his whole body.
In the facts and circumstances, it would be appropriate to presume that the petitioner is suffering from 50% disability with respect to his whole body.
Since the petitioner was a minor, therefore, it could be safely assumed that he was accompanied by his parents/ guardian.
He also suffered a permanent disability to the extent of 75% from psychiatry side.
However, since the offending vehicle was insured with R-3 at the time of accident, therefore, R-3/ Insurance Company is liable to indemnify R-2 in respect of above liability.
